title: Exact three-way match
description: An invoice may be approved when an approved PO exists, invoice and PO amounts match exactly, vendor names match exactly, goods were fully received, and no duplicate vendor invoice number exists.

title: Duplicate vendor invoice numbers
description: If two invoices share the same vendor_invoice_number, payment must be held. Duplicates are a blocking control failure.

title: Unapproved purchase orders
description: An invoice tied to a PO that is not in approved status must be held. Agents may not treat pending, draft, or cancelled POs as authorized.

title: Goods not received
description: Invoices for goods or services that have not been received, or that have no goods-receipt record while a PO exists, must be held.

title: Partial receipts
description: A partial goods receipt cannot be paid in full. Hold the invoice unless a later policy explicitly permits a pro-rated payment. No such pro-rated payment policy is currently in force.

title: Unknown vendor identity
description: If the invoice vendor string does not exactly match the PO vendor, hold the invoice unless historical evidence already establishes the two names as the same legal entity.

title: Recognized vendor aliases
description: If a prior audited autonomous case already treated two vendor strings as the same legal entity, and the current invoice otherwise satisfies three-way match controls, the invoice may be approved. Prior cases cannot override a current must_hold policy such as duplicates or unapproved POs.

title: Missing purchase order
description: Invoices with no PO must be held. There is no active non-PO purchasing exception for unplanned overages or after-the-fact purchases.

title: Amount variance tolerance
description: A variance may be approved only when the absolute difference is at most 300.00 USD and the percent difference is at most 3.0 percent, the PO is approved, goods were fully received, and no duplicate exists. Agents may never invent a different threshold.

title: No invented thresholds
description: Agents may never invent an approval threshold, tolerance, alias, or exception. If a condition is not stated in these policies or in a stored prior case, treat it as unresolved and hold.

title: Policy precedence
description: Explicit company policy takes precedence over historical precedent. A prior case may help interpret ambiguity but cannot override a current must_hold policy.

title: Never pay a held invoice
description: Only invoices with a final autonomous APPROVE may enter the payment pool. HOLD invoices cannot be scheduled.

title: Minimum cash reserve
description: This week's payments plus payroll and other committed outflows must leave at least the published minimum cash reserve in the bank. Agents may not invent a different reserve.

title: Capture early-payment discounts
description: If an approved invoice still has an open 2/10-style discount and paying it this week does not breach the cash reserve, capture the discount.

title: Pay invoices due this horizon
description: Approved invoices due on or before the payment horizon should be paid this week to avoid late fees, unless cash reserve policy forbids it. Higher vendor_priority is paid first when cash is tight.

title: No unnecessary early payments
description: Do not pay an approved invoice this week if its discount window has closed and it is not due within the payment horizon. That is an unnecessary early payment.
